svg.title: Fieldnotes — private places, one note per place
svg.desc: Fieldnotes event-storming board. One Fieldnotes bounded context, five command groups handled by Place, resulting domain events, typed business rejections and one projection. A separate gray integration band shows direct Google or Firebase sign-in and application-session logout; these are not Place domain events.

text.tspan: Private places. One Markdown note per place.
Read each group left to right. Large labels explain the action; monospace labels name the message or state.
One Place aggregate holds a position, a name, one Markdown body, its author and a version.
Verified author required before access. Commands, queries, subscriptions and results are scoped to that author.
Repeated yellow cards show the same Aggregate type; each saved Place is a separate consistency boundary.
One save records the pin, name and initial note together.
Changes the name shown beside the pin; keeps the same note.
Updates coordinates on the same place; the note moves with it.
Replaces the one Markdown body. Never adds a second note.
Removes the place and its note from visible results together.
PlaceView: one record per saved place, including its Markdown.
The map, places list, reading panel and editor use the same view.
The write commits first; event subscriptions update views afterward.
Editable fields and their version describe the same saved revision.
Read/Preview, search, pan, zoom and selection emit no domain event.
Red notes are typed business refusals, not network/login errors.
Invalid coordinates are refused before handling.
Unknown, deleted or another person’s ID receives the same
PlaceUnavailable response, including conflicting AddPlace input.
PlaceAlreadyExists is disclosed only for an accessible Place.
A stale edit keeps the draft visible so the author can reconcile it.
AUTHENTICATION & ACCESS / TECHNICAL INTEGRATION — OUTSIDE THE BUSINESS CONTEXT
Two launch options, one interface. Gray steps are authentication operations, not Place Commands or Events.
Sign in with Google through Firebase Auth
Same application session strategy in both launches
Use the verified author; never trust a browser-supplied user ID.
Apply it to commands, reads, live updates and outcomes.
Revoke this application session → clear cookie / SDK state → stop protected streams best effort.
Technical note: direct Google uses OIDC; Firebase uses server-verified tokens. Both issue persistent Spine sessions.
Expiry is deployment configuration; later Firebase revocation is not immediate. No email-based linking. One Spine host.
One note value per saved PlaceId, even if empty. Multiple saved pins at the same coordinates are allowed for any author.
Delete removes current content from use; event-history and backup erasure require a separate retention policy.
Single-tenant application, multiple private users. Domain design for the approved Fieldnotes implementation.
